manualSections.heading: 🧩 x-button + x-* behavior composition
manualSections.html:
Any x-* behavior (ripple, tooltip, toast, etc.) composes onto a button the same way it does onto any other element — stack as many as you want, in any order, with no wrapper behaviors.

Each x- attribute adds one capability to the button — no JavaScript.

  • x-ripplematerial-style ripple on click
  • x-tooltiphover hint, positionable
  • x-toastfires a toast notification
  • x-copycopies text to the clipboard
  • x-wobblewobble animation
  • x-tadatada celebration animation

Stack multiple x- attributes on one button — they layer, they don't conflict.

🧩 x-help — permanent hint text
manualSections.html:
x-help is for hint text a user should see without hovering or interacting — a short instruction that sits permanently under a field ("must be 8+ characters"). If the text should only appear on hover/focus, use x-tooltip instead — the two are deliberately kept separate.

Find this in your account settings under "Developer".

🎨 Native Semantic Elements — x-* on plain HTML
manualSections.html:
Enhanced form controls using standard HTML elements with x-* behaviors.

Button <button>

The loading/icon/icon-position attributes only work on the <x-button> custom tag — a native <button> only maps size/variant to styling classes.

Input <input>

Textarea <textarea>

Checkbox & Radio

checkbox has no label attribute of its own — wrap it in a real <label>.

Switch

Known gap (#322): <x-switch> needs its schema built before it can render — that never happens on this page's runtime (wb-lazy.js, used by every standalone demo page), so it won't render here yet. This markup is the correct API; it works today on the main site (?page=behaviors).

Rating

icon takes a literal emoji character, not a keyword — icon="heart" renders the literal text "heart", not ❤️. precision isn't a real attribute (not read anywhere in rating.js).

Select <select>

Range <input type="range">

Form <form>

x-form has no loading-text option (that only exists in an unregistered alternate implementation).

manualSections.heading: 🎨 Theme & Dark Mode
manualSections.html:
Behaviors for managing themes and dark mode.

Theme Control x-themecontrol

A dropdown to switch the global theme. Persists selection to localStorage.

Forced Theme x-darkmode

These sections have forced themes regardless of the global setting. target="self" scopes the theme to the element itself; theme="…" sets which theme (not data-theme, which x-darkmode doesn't read).

Forced Dark Mode

This card will always be dark.

Forced Light Mode

This card will always be light.

Forced Cyberpunk

This card will always be cyberpunk.

Nested Themes

Themes cascade through data-theme on any container — no behavior needed, just the plain HTML attribute the theme system itself keys off of. A nested container can override its ancestor's theme.

Forest Theme Container

This container uses data-theme="forest" directly in HTML.

Inherited Forest Card

Nested Sunset Card

Overriding parent theme with data-theme="sunset".
